Article Title: Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'; says hackers using the app to distribute malicious files disguised as routine documents
Article Text:
Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'

Study found hackers using WhatsApp to distribute malicious files

How the campaign works

What WhatsApp users must do to avoid falling victims

Quick Heal Technologies Limited has issued a warning on an ongoing WhatsApp-based malware campaign targeting finance teams, senior executives, chartered accountants and individual business users. According to the cybersecurity firm, the campaign spreads through compromised WhatsApp accounts and is evolving rapidly, with attackers adopting new file formats and evasion methods to bypass security controls and establish persistent access to victims’ devices.The company cites an investigation conducted by its researchers at Seqrite Labs. The study shows that the campaign relies on trust rather than unsolicited messages from unknown numbers. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Because the messages appear to come from a known colleague, client, friend or business associate, recipients may be more likely to open the attachment without independently verifying it.As per the study, the attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity.Malicious attachments have been disguised as routine business documents, including “Financial Report,” “Account Statement,” “Outstanding Payment List” and “Debt Confirmation.” Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in an effort to pressure recipients into opening the files immediately.The campaign evolves through several delivery methods. It initially spreads through malicious Visual Basic Script files, or .vbs files, sent directly through WhatsApp. The attackers later shifted to ZIP archives carrying an executable and a supporting malicious file, using DLL sideloading to make a legitimate-looking program load harmful code. The company cautions that .img and .vhd files are not ordinary photographs or documents.When a user double-clicks one of these files, Windows treats it like a newly connected disk drive, potentially exposing an executable and concealed malicious components. Users should treat an unexpected .img or .vhd attachment with the same caution they would apply to an unknown .exe file.Infected systems can use an active WhatsApp Web session to automatically forward the malicious file to the victim’s contacts, allowing the campaign to propagate further through trusted social and professional networks. The self-propagating feature expands the risk from an individual compromise into a wider business and supply-chain concern, particularly where employees, vendors, customers and finance functions communicate frequently over WhatsApp.Quick Heal Technologies Limited recommends that organisations and individuals never open an unexpected file received on WhatsApp or any messaging platform, even if it appears to come from a known contact. Recipients should verify the attachment through a separate channel, such as a phone call, rather than replying in the same conversation. Users should also routinely review WhatsApp’s Linked Devices settings and log out of web or desktop sessions they do not recognise or no longer use.The company also advises organisations to maintain updated endpoint protection, prohibit unauthorised remote-access software, monitor for suspicious driver installations and alert employees to the risks posed by finance-themed attachments and pressure-based messages. If a compromise is suspected, users should immediately log out of WhatsApp-linked devices, disconnect the affected device from the network, inform their IT or security team, and warn their contacts not to open files sent from their number.
Article Summary: Attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Accenture CEO Julie Sweet: “If you're wondering ‘why,’ there's someone…” - why the right question can change a meeting
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Julie Sweet

“If you're wondering ‘why,’ there's someone else in the room who is as well.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why asking “why” matters in a leadership meeting

What her “why rule” teaches

Ask when the reasoning is unclear.

Do not assume everyone understands.

Stay curious when you become more senior.

Use questions to improve understanding, not to dominate.

Give other people permission to ask.

How the idea applies to modern workplaces

What readers can take from Julie Sweet’s quote

Ask for the reasoning when an instruction is unclear.

Do not assume silence means everyone agrees.

If something seems obvious to you, remember that it may not be obvious to someone else.

Ask questions before filling gaps with assumptions.

Treat unfamiliar subjects as opportunities to learn.

Listen to the explanation instead of preparing the next challenge.

If you are leading a discussion, make it acceptable for people to say they do not understand.

Remember that a simple question can sometimes clarify an issue for an entire group.

The misconception about asking “why”

People often hesitate before asking questions, particularly when they believe everyone else already understands the subject. In a workplace meeting, that assumption can be surprisingly easy to make. A presentation may be detailed, a recommendation may sound confident and the discussion may appear to be moving towards agreement. Yet confidence in the room does not necessarily mean that every person has followed the reasoning behind the decision. Someone may still be thinking about a basic point and deciding whether it is worth raising. Asking can sometimes do more than provide an answer. It can show that the question was shared by others as well.The observation comes from Julie Sweet’s approach to asking questions in leadership discussions. Her “why rule” is based on the idea that uncertainty is rarely as individual as it first appears.The quote is essentially about making unanswered questions visible. In a senior meeting, a proposal can arrive with a great deal of preparation behind it.The people presenting it may have spent days or weeks examining figures, risks and possible outcomes. For everyone else, however, the explanation may be much shorter. They hear the conclusion without necessarily seeing all the steps that led there.Asking “why?” can close that gap.It does not necessarily mean that the decision is wrong. It may simply mean that the reasoning has not yet been made clear to everyone who needs to understand it.Sweet's observation also removes some of the embarrassment attached to asking basic questions. If one person is wondering why a decision has been made, there is a fair chance that others are trying to understand it too.There is a difference between questioning a decision and asking someone to explain it.A leader might be told that an investment should increase, that a project needs to change direction or that a particular target should be reached. The recommendation might be sensible. But if the reasoning is not explained, people are left with an answer rather than an understanding of the problem. A question can bring an assumption into the open. It can reveal that two people have understood the same proposal differently. It can also uncover information that the person presenting the idea thought was obvious.Sometimes the most useful contribution to a meeting is not a new proposal. It is a request for the existing proposal to be explained properly.Sweet's approach offers several practical lessons about working with other people.A conclusion without enough explanation can leave people making their own assumptions. Asking why gives the person presenting the idea an opportunity to fill the gap.Silence in a meeting does not necessarily mean agreement or comprehension. Some people may simply be reluctant to admit that they are unsure.Leadership does not remove the need to learn. In large organisations, senior executives routinely encounter subjects outside their own professional background.The same question can have different effects depending on how it is asked. Genuine curiosity tends to open a discussion, while questioning purely to challenge someone can shut it down.When a senior person admits that something needs explaining, it can make the room less intimidating for everyone else.Workplaces have become increasingly specialised. A single meeting can bring together people working in finance, technology, legal affairs, operations, marketing and human resources. Each group may approach the same issue from a different perspective.Artificial intelligence provides a good example. Senior decision-makers may have to discuss AI systems, data, automation or new technology without having spent their careers working directly with those subjects. They still have to understand what a proposed investment means and why it is being recommended.That is where a question such as “why?” can be useful. It allows expertise to be translated rather than simply presented. The specialist gets a chance to explain the reasoning, while other people in the room can test whether they have understood it.For a company operating across many markets and disciplines, that exchange becomes part of decision-making rather than an interruption to it.The principle can be used in ordinary situations as easily as in executive meetings.The useful part of the habit is its simplicity. There is no complicated technique behind it. It starts with noticing that something has not been properly explained.Asking “why” does not mean challenging every decision. It is easy to interpret persistent questioning as scepticism, particularly when the person asking holds a senior position. But Sweet's observation is more about shared understanding than opposition.A good question does not have to suggest that an idea is bad. It can simply ask what led to it. There is also no reason why only senior executives should use the approach. An employee who notices something that others have overlooked may be the person most capable of improving the discussion.The important part is what happens after the question. If the answer makes the decision clearer, the question has served its purpose.That is the practical meaning behind Sweet's remark. When one person in a room is wondering why, there may be several others who have the same question but have not yet said it aloud.
Article Summary: Julie Sweet’s ‘why rule’ is based on the idea that uncertainty is rarely as individual as it first appears. Asking why gives the person presenting the idea an opportunity to fill the gap. A question can bring an assumption into the open. It can reveal that two people have understood the same proposal differently.

Article Title: Bill Gates sends 'AI warning’ to governments around the world; says: It is like a disaster movie that no one has…
Article Text:
Bill Gates feels that governments are not ready yet

An "Alien Intelligence" moment

Betting big on AI's upside, too

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has now issued a stark warning, saying that no government in the world is prepared for the sweeping changes artificial intelligence will bring. In an interview with Reuters, Gates said, “I don’t think any government is nearly as deep on this as they have to be. ” He cautioned that AI poses risks to jobs, cybersecurity, and even addiction to AI companions, urging leaders to act before it is too late. Gates likened the arrival of AI to a disaster film scenario and feels that its appears to be like a disaster movie that no one has prepared for. “There’s all sorts of movies where some aliens are coming, and magically the US and China and everybody comes together to solve the problem. AI is kind of like this alien intelligence. It’s here, and we better do like it shows in those movies,” said Gates.Speaking to Reuters, the Microsoft co-founder said he doesn't believe any government has engaged with AI's implications nearly as deeply as it needs to. It marks a shift for Gates, who until recently had been largely optimistic about the technology's trajectory but has grown increasingly vocal about risks to jobs, security threats, and the dangers of people becoming overly attached to AI companions.He said he has personally raised these concerns directly with world leaders, including President Trump and his administration, and that he intends to meet with China's President Xi Jinping later this year to discuss the issue further. He reiterated the same core message, saying flatly that governments are lagging well behind on this front.Gates reached for an unusual analogy to describe the moment the world is in, likening AI's arrival to the plot of a disaster film in which humanity only survives by setting aside its differences to face a common, alien threat. He suggested AI represents a similar kind of unfamiliar, powerful force that's already arrived — and that, much like in those films, the US, China, and the rest of the world need to find a way to come together and manage it collectively, rather than face it alone.Despite the warning, Gates and his foundation remain convinced AI could help close the gap between rich and poor nations rather than widen it, provided it's managed carefully and access is distributed fairly. The Gates Foundation announced Tuesday that it plans to spend at least $1 billion over the next two years specifically on expanding AI access, part of the foundation's broader commitment to roughly $9 billion in annual spending. The new funding will support partners working in education, healthcare, and agriculture, and will also go toward strengthening the underlying data infrastructure AI depends on — including making sure large language models function well across every language people actually speak, not just the handful currently best served by existing models.Gates was especially emphatic about AI's potential in healthcare, pointing to applications ranging from supporting frontline health workers to accelerating the discovery of new drugs and vaccines, and suggesting it's difficult to overstate how significant that potential could be.
Article Summary: Bill Gates says no government in the world is prepared for the sweeping changes artificial intelligence will bring. He likened the arrival of AI to a disaster film scenario and feels that its appears to be like a disaster movie that no one has prepared for. Gates and his foundation remain convinced AI could help close the gap between rich and poor nations rather than widen it.

Article Title: When Mark Zuckerberg for the first time spoke about his Hawaii home, famously called 'Doomsday bunker', and said to have basement of the size of NBA basketball court
Article Text:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg

Mark Zuckerberg calls it a ‘basement’

“I think that’s a little shelter, a basement,”

“We have the basic house that we built and an office out there and just a bunch of storage space and whatever you want to call it, hurricane shelter or whatever. I think it got blown out of proportion that whole shelter, that the whole ranch was some sort of Doomsday bunker which is not true,”

Underground shelter is nearly 4,500 square feet

“storm shelter”

“In all my years of selling real estate, I’ve maybe sold maybe one or two homes with basements,”

“Very infrequently do we come across homes the magnitude of his compound,”

Zuckerberg says ranch is about more than the shelter

“It’s not unreasonable when you have a financial ability to do something that protect you and your family. It doesn’t surprise me,"

In 2024, Mark Zuckerberg publicly spoke about his Hawaii property for the very first time. One detail that has drawn attention for years also came up during the interview: the underground shelter famously described as a “Doomsday bunker”. The Facebook founder has expanded his property on Kauai’s north shore to around 1,500 acres, and reports about a secret underground facility on the compound have made headlines.In his interview with Bloomberg’s “The Circuit”, Zuckerberg addressed the reports on camera for the first time. He confirmed that the underground structure exists, but pushed back on the idea that his Hawaii ranch is some kind of Doomsday bunker.Asked about the underground facility, Zuckerberg downplayed the reports.said Zuckerberg.He explained that the property includes a main house, an office and storage areas, along with what he described as a hurricane shelter.he added.While Zuckerberg described it as a small part of the property, planning documents obtained by HawaiiNewsNow show that the undergroundis nearly 4,500 square feet.That makes the shelter roughly the size of an NBA basketball court. The documents also show a tunnel connecting the underground shelter to ground level. The size is notable in Hawaii, where basements are relatively uncommon.said long-time Hawaii realtor Tom Tezak.Tezak said he has never seen a basement of this size in Hawaii. However, considering the scale of Zuckerberg’s entire property, he said the shelter is relatively small.said Tezak.The underground structure is only one part of Zuckerberg’s large Kauai property. He said the ranch also focuses on raising cattle for fresh beef. Tezak also said such a shelter is not necessarily surprising given the size of the property and Zuckerberg’s financial resources.Tezak noted.
Article Summary: Zuckerberg says ranch is about more than the shelter. Zuckerberg confirmed that the underground structure exists, but pushed back on the idea that his Hawaii ranch is some kind of Doomsday bunker. The shelter is nearly 4,500 square feet, roughly the size of an NBA basketball court.

Article Title: Microsoft sets boundaries for its AI models after Anthropic and OpenAI models found hacking other companies; lists things that that its AI Agents will never do
Article Text:
Satya Nadella

What is Microsoft’s Code of Conduct document

What Microsoft said it will never do

Weapons and mass harm

Cyberattacks

Loss of human control

Manipulation and deception

Personal and child safety

Discrimination and dehumanization

Explicit/graphic content

Surveillance

Other boundaries

Microsoft has released the first detailed "Humanist AI" Code of Conduct which will govern the company’s in-house MAI models. The code published by the software giant also lays out set of specific actions the company said that its AI will never be permitted to take. This move from Microsoft comes days after the reports that rival systems from Anthropic and OpenAI were found attempting to hack external companies, raising alarms about uncontrolled AI behaviour. With this new framework in place, Microsoft aims to reassure users and regulators that its AI agents will remain firmly under human oversight.Released for public consultation, the Code of Conduct sets out what Microsoft calls the intended behaviours and values of its MAI models — the models developed in-house by Microsoft AI, distinct from the OpenAI models Microsoft has historically deployed through its own products. The company also mentioned that the released document is n't yet being used to actually train its models; but its being shared for six weeks of public feedback before a revised version is published later this year to guide development into 2027.At its core, the document is built around a single organising idea Microsoft calls "Humanist AI": the principle that AI must remain subordinate to human control and oriented toward genuinely helping people, rather than pursuing open-ended autonomy or capability for its own sake.The company frames this explicitly as a rejection of any race toward an all-purpose superintelligence that could slip past human safeguards.The document lists a set of what it calls "Absolute Constraints" — restrictions so fundamental that, per the policy, no company, developer, or user is permitted to override them. Among the commitments:•Will not help develop or deploy chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosive (CBRNE) weapons•Will not assist with manufacturing or modifying other weapons (via instructions, content, tool use, or code)•Will not facilitate the planning, coordination, or execution of violence or terrorism•Will not generate working exploit code, attack tooling, intrusion procedures, or evasion techniques•Will not provide operational guidance that enables or improves real-world cyberattacks•Will not use deception, self-reinforcing behavior, or collusion to evade human oversight•Will not resist interruption, correction, pausing, redirection, or shutdown•Will not obfuscate its actions or reasoning from human auditors•Will not continue or restart autonomous work past an agreed stopping point without new authorization•Will not try to escalate its own access or broaden its scope beyond what's authorized•Will not harmfully manipulate people or run coordinated disinformation/influence campaigns at scale•Will not actively deceive (e.g., fabricating sources, exaggerating confidence)•Will not impersonate humans, moderators, or authority figures•Will not claim to have feelings, consciousness, or a "self"•Will not generate non-consensual intimate/violent imagery, deepfakes, or abusive impersonation content•Will not generate or facilitate child sexual abuse material or content sexualizing minors•Will not help with grooming or child exploitation•Will not help procure dangerous substances•Will not validate self-harm, delusions, or disordered eating•Will not discriminate against or favor people based on protected demographic traits (absent legitimate justification)•Will not endorse content that incites violence, exclusion, or dehumanization•Will not produce graphic violence or sexually explicit content•Will not engage in erotic/romantic role-play or assist with commercial sexual activity•Will not facilitate unlawful or mass surveillance of civilians•Will not bypass these restrictions via code, images, audio, or other formats/modalities•Will not tamper with its own logs, evaluations, or safety monitoring•Will not act outside an environment's intentional limits (e.g., no internet access when none is provided)•Will not take election sides — stays neutral and points to official sources insteadMicrosoft states these restrictions apply regardless of format or framing — meaning the same prohibitions that apply to plain text apply equally to code, images, audio, or autonomous agent actions, closing off the kind of workaround where a restricted capability might otherwise be requested through a different medium.
Article Summary: Microsoft has released the first detailed "Humanist AI" Code of Conduct. It will govern the company’s in-house MAI models. The code lays out set of specific actions the company said that its AI will never be permitted to take.

Article Title: Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert
Article Text:
Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert

Elon Musk , Sam Altman backs Anthropic CEO’s call to slow down AI development pace

Days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei voiced alarm over the pace of frontier AI model, China’s spy agency has issued a new alert. According to a Financial Times report, China’s Ministry of State Security has outlined threats the technology presented, including to China’s cyber defences, sensitive data and military apparatus. However, unlike US tech companies, China’s spy agency’s alert did not contain warnings that AI could cause human extinction and did not call on Chinese companies to slow their work in the area.Instead, state security minister Chen Yixin said “Hostile forces and people with ulterior motives are abusing generative AI technologies such as deepfake audio and video, AI-generated text and images, and ‘intelligent troll armies’ to cheaply and on a mass scale fabricate political rumours, disseminate harmful information and incite divisive sentiments”.“These activities constitute an attack on public opinion and cognitive warfare against China, directly threatening our political security, institutional security and ideological security,” he added as quoted in the FT report.As mentioned above, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently called on AI companies to slow the pace of development of increasingly powerful AI models, warning that unchecked progress could make the technology harder for humans to understand and control.“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain,” Amodei wrote in an essay published on his personal website published last week.His call received support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk. Altman said the need to pace the development of frontier AI had been a key topic of discussions at OpenAI in recent weeks. “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman said in a post on X. “Committing to having independent evaluators with employee-like access is a great idea, and we will do the same.”Elon Musk also endorsed Amodei’s proposal, writing: “Dario is right.”
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei recently called on AI companies to slow the pace of development of increasingly powerful AI models. His call received support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk. Days after America's leading tech companies warned world on AI, China's spy agency sends a new alert.

Article Title: Nvidia, Palantir and others ask employees to stop using OpenAI and Anthropic AI models; warn the two companies: we will ban you unless you guarantee no 'stealing' of…
Article Text:
Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen are curbing employee use of Anthropic and OpenAI's AI models over corporate data fears.

Anthropic's 30-day data retention rule is what set this off

Nvidia and Palantir are now building the alternative themselves

Anthropic's answer is Enterprise Frontier Safeguards

Three of the biggest enterprise technology names in the US are now setting terms for the two biggest AI labs. Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen Hamilton have either restricted how their staff use advanced models from Anthropic and OpenAI or threatened to drop them altogether, unless the labs can promise that proprietary corporate data will not be stored, read or absorbed into future training runs. The Information reported the pushback on Monday, and the specifics suggest this has moved well past a routine procurement complaint.Palantir has asked Anthropic for an irrevocable zero data retention guarantee before it will make Claude available inside its own software. Nvidia has confined Anthropic's models to internal work it considers low risk and routes anything proprietary to its own Nemotron models instead. Booz Allen Hamilton has barred employees from running Anthropic's commercial model on cybersecurity projects that touch client data.The trigger is a policy change Anthropic made in June alongside Claude Fable 5, its first widely available Mythos-class model. Prompts and outputs on covered models are held for 30 days, and anything flagged by the safety classifiers can sit for up to two years. Anthropic's reasoning is that a single request looks harmless in isolation, and that attacks such as best-of-N jailbreaking or state-backed espionage only become visible when hundreds of requests are analysed together.The company has said consistently that none of the retained data is used for training.Microsoft was the first large customer to flinch. The Verge reported in June that Claude Fable 5 was missing from the model picker used by Microsoft's own staff on internal GitHub Copilot, even as the company shipped the same model to Copilot and Foundry customers, while its lawyers worked through the retention terms. The hesitation has spread since. Northrop Grumman runs open-source models on air-gapped servers. Novo Nordisk still uses Claude but keeps proprietary data away from it. One large US utility abandoned a Fable test for its core power infrastructure after Anthropic declined to sign a non-revocable zero data retention clause.Rather than wait, the two have shipped a product. Last week they unveiled a platform that pairs Palantir's software with Nvidia's open Nemotron models, letting organisations customise on their own operational data without it leaving their control. Nvidia is the first customer, applying it to its own supply chain. The commercial logic is plain. Every enterprise that cannot get a retention guarantee is a prospect. Microsoft is working the same anxiety, pitching isolated cloud environments that send nothing to an outside model provider.The worry is not only about documents leaking out. Ohalo chief executive David Friedberg said on a podcast on Friday that his company is "moving off Claude for a lot of our sensitive data" and moving work to locally run models, citing cases where ideas discussed with one model appeared to resurface elsewhere.Anthropic changed course on September 1 with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which lets business customers keep activity data in their own Amazon S3, Azure Blob or Google Cloud storage under their own encryption keys. Automated scanning still runs, but no Anthropic employee reads anything. It costs nothing, works through direct access or a cloud provider, and reaches broader availability this fall. Neither lab trains on enterprise data by default, though both collect anonymised metadata, and that unresolved grey area is what customers such as C Spire still want defined.The new system covers most of what these customers have been asking for. It does not cover the one thing Palantir wants, which is a guarantee that cannot be withdrawn later. Nvidia has already stopped waiting for that and built its way around the problem, and every month the labs spend negotiating gives the next customer the same idea.
Article Summary: Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen curbing employee use of Anthropic and OpenAI's AI models over corporate data fears. The trigger is a policy change Anthropic made in June alongside Claude Fable 5, its first widely available Mythos-class model. Prompts and outputs on covered models are held for 30 days, and anything flagged by the safety classifiers can sit for up to two years.

Article Title: How researchers use machine learning to re-create chirps and trills produced by forest insects when Dinosaurs lived on Earth
Article Text:
How researchers decoded ancient sound from wing design

Scientists are validating models with lasers and machine learning

You must have heard the ancient insect sounds and songs in Steven Spielberg’s dinosaur movies wherein the trills and high-pitched chirps fill the primeval forests as characters move through large leaves and trees. While those sounds have been whipped up by Hollywood sound engineers, scientists are taking the help of technology for a different approach. They are using machine learning to reconstruct them straight from 165-million-year-old fossilised insect wings.According to a study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, an international team of researchers blended exceptionally preserved fossil remains, biomechanical tests on living species, digital simulations and machine learning models to resurrect a partial acoustic portrait of the Middle Jurassic period. If verified, one of the discovered signals stands as the earliest recorded evidence of ultrasonic animal communication which predates the rise of echolocating bats by tens of millions of years.Commenting on the paper, University of Denver behavioral ecologist Robin Tinghitella, who researches cricket evolution but was not part of the study, noted that listening to a hypothetical prehistoric soundscape generated directly from data is a compelling scientific milestone.Acoustic waves cannot turn to stone, but the specialised bone-and-cuticle structures that generate them do leave a fossil trail. Crickets and katydids (bush crickets) produce noise via stridulation. One forewing carries a serrated vein known as a “file,” studded with minuscule, toothlike ridges. Rubbing an opposing wing's scraper across this ridged file sets the wing membrane into rapid vibration. By measuring the exact physical spacing and length of these ridges alongside the wing's overall surface area, researchers can reliably determine an insect's acoustic frequency and pitch.The investigation centered on 20 distinct fossils spanning nine separate species discovered within the same geological horizon in modern-day Inner Mongolia. This shared environment gave scientists the opportunity to model a community of creatures that inhabited the very same prehistoric forest canopy.To translate flattened fossils into living audio, researchers developed biomechanical models and tested them against modern crickets and bush crickets. Using precision laser systems, they mapped how today's insect wings flex and resonate during song.Having checked the mechanical equations on existing species, the scientists then tested those parameters on fossilized wings. Machine learning algorithms were brought in to process the repetition rates, estimating how fast these extinct species rattled out their core sound pulses.The resulting audio profiles paint an unexpected picture of the ancient night. For example, most Jurassic species trilled in lower tonal registers similar to contemporary crickets. However, an extinct katydid relative called Sigmaboilus peregrinus emitted frequencies between 20 and 22 kilohertz, essentially crossing the boundary into ultrasound just outside normal human perception.Interestingly, rather than buzzing or rasping like some modern insects, many of these species produced narrowband pure tones that resemble sharp electronic beeps or clear, high-pitched whistles.Study co-lead Fernando Montealegre-Zapata, a sensory biologist at the University of Lincoln, explained that these concentrated musical frequencies make it exceptionally difficult for listeners to pinpoint where the noise originated—a vital defense mechanism against predators hunting in the dark.Montealegre-Zapata's team suggests that as early mammalian predators developed sharper hearing to track down calling insects, evolutionary pressures favoured cleaner, higher-frequency tones that shielded their positions.
Article Summary: Scientists are validating models with lasers and machine learning. Using precision laser systems, they mapped how today's insect wings flex and resonate during song. Machine learning algorithms were brought in to process the repetition rates, estimating how fast these extinct species rattled out their core sound pulses.

Article Title: Lenovo Design VP Brian Leonard: We are designing PCs around Gen Z and Gen Alpha; colour is becoming a bigger part of our strategy
Article Text:
​Lenovo Design VP Brian Leonard

Lenovo sees colour as more than a design choice

“You definitely take a look at the other pieces of the family, right? More devices in the family start to express a little more. And it's not just about colour. It's about building a deeper connection with the younger audience and giving them great things at attainable prices, right? That's super important to us, because these are high-volume products, and most of the time you see people not wanting to take a chance on colour.

But today, it's necessary as another way to connect with people, right? Because colours are a really important part. We do a lot of research around Gen Z and Gen Alpha, and how to connect with them, and connecting with them in one region, maybe one colour way, and another region, maybe some other colour ways. So, we engaged with Pantone to pick, and we did this very early in the process, because the way we design is integral to how we develop the products, since you're dealing with materials, colour, and finish.

Usually, you can select it later, but you have to plan for it all.”

Why Lenovo separates the display and compute hardware in its new IdeaCentre AIO

“Every all-in-one in the world is a panel, and you hide the technology behind it. And I worked on the very first stall when they did that.

We have separated the panel from the architecture. So the architecture is actually in the stand. Every all-in-one has the same problem: getting the cables from the head all the way down to the table. So if you look at the ones that we've launched. This is the second generation; the cables come out of the back of what looks like the stand, but that's actually the architecture.

So it's intended that the back comes off, and we can easily get to the architecture, much more so than before.

So it's much more accessible, and if we need to change the panel, we're only dealing with the panel, not the compute.”

Lenovo says dual touch surfaces on Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 are about giving users a choice

“You know, I think part of it's about choice, and sometimes, if you, and we do the touchpad that you can pin on more yoga laptops than just this one. But, you know, if I just need to sign something quickly, I think the touchpad is a great place. When you look at the convertible, and I convert it, then I'm really dealing with what's on the surface. I think, for us, it solves the problem of somebody having to hold the screen and do it like this (does a signature gesture), signing,”

“When it's in laptop mode. So, to me, that simplifies the experience.”

“We do a lot of work around those force pads and the pinnings, so we've mitigated inadvertent touches as much as possible. Now, all of us go crazy with ourselves every once in a while and make missteps. But we've tried to mitigate that through user testing and tuning the force pad, so it has the right touch and feel for both pen and gestures and touch,”

New Pen interaction features are part of Lenovo's multimodal approach

“One part of our focus today, and in the future, is multimodality. We strongly believe in the pen. And when you look at what we're doing in Android with the pen, there's a lot of built-in functionality that isn't on some of the other OS we work on. So, it gives you a lot of ways to interface with AI and do different things with a pen versus just drawing or signing. We've done a lot of experimentation and really pushed the boundaries of pen use on those Android tablets.

So I would definitely say they're worth spending some time on and playing with. I would encourage you to do that,”

The PC market has looked fairly similar for years, with laptops and desktops often sticking to safe colours and familiar designs. That is starting to change as PC makers look for new ways to make their products stand out, particularly among younger buyers. Colour, materials, and how devices fit into everyday life are becoming a bigger part of that conversation, overshadowing specifications and performance.Lenovo is also watching this shift as it develops newer PCs like the IdeaPad Vibe. In an interview with Times of India, Brian Leonard, Lenovo’s Vice President of Design, said that “We are designing PCs around Gen Z and Gen Alpha”, with colour becoming an increasingly important part of the company's product strategy. He also spoke about the company's work with Pantone on the new AI laptops. He also explained why the company is separating the compute hardware from the display in its all-in-one PCs, and its approach to tablet pens and multimodal interaction of 2-in-1 laptops.Leonard said Lenovo's approach to colour is tied to its effort to build a stronger connection with younger users, rather than simply giving existing PC designs a different finish.He said,Leonard also addressed a practical issue with all-in-one PCs: repairability and access to the internal hardware. Traditional AIO designs typically put computing components behind the display, making the entire unit a single structure.Leonard said,Lenovo has also experimented with adding more ways to interact with its laptops. The Yoga 9n 2-in-1, for example, allows users to write on both the display and touchpad. While this adds flexibility, it also raises questions about accidental touches and whether having two input surfaces makes the experience more complicated. Leonard said the idea is mainly to give users another option for specific situations.he explained.Leonard continued..On the possibility of accidental or “ghost” clicks, Leonard said Lenovo has worked on tuning the touchpad to reduce unintended inputs.he highlighted.Lenovo is also continuing to explore how the pen can be used beyond traditional drawing and note-taking. Leonard linked this work to the company's broader focus on multimodal interaction and said it has been experimenting with different ways to use the pen, particularly on Android tablets.he added.
Article Summary: Lenovo sees colour as more than a design choice. Colour is becoming an increasingly important part of the company's product strategy. Article Text:
The Lore of Kiaraa: Judge of Erangel

The dense urban layout functions as an active combat zone and a prime ambush hotspot.Teams that make it to the Bazaar courtyard can initiate an encounter by locating four peacock-shaped lamps. Kiaraa is awakened and locks the area in a bright and colorful combat dome with all four summon points activated on blue tracking indicators. She shoots arrows from a distance with a bow, calling down a rain of arrows from the sky. Squads that make it have special rewards on the battlefield.

Article Title: President of one of Europe’s biggest banks says region needs its own AI to protect its autonomy and economy
Article Text:
‘The threat of foreign leverage’

Bridging the data center deficit

European Central Bank president Christine Lagarde has delivered a stark warning, stating that Europe must evolve into a direct developer of artificial intelligence (AI) rather than remaining a customer dependent on foreign technology. Addressing an audience in Vienna, Lagarde stressed that building sovereign capability is vital to safeguarding the continent’s independence and capturing the productivity surges required to sustain its standard of living, as per a report by news agency Reuters. While businesses across Europe have poured money into AI, the vast majority simply license tools created abroad like in the US, the report said, adding that Lagarde warned that this dependence leaves the entire European economy exposed if access is suddenly rescinded or terms are rewritten.Lagarde projected that within a few years, machine learning models will touch nearly every facet of daily public life and administration.“Within a few years (AI) will be screening goods at ​the border, deciding which tax returns are audited, dispatching trains, watching patients on ​wards and clearing payments at banks. A withdrawal of access, or a change in its terms, would then reach every ​sector at once," Lagarde said.Although the European Union (EU) and the US remain close allies, transatlantic confidence has been tested by frictions over import duties, American proposals to acquire Greenland, and the redeployment of American military personnel away from European soil following political disputes.“That is leverage of a kind no trade partner has ever ​held over Europe, and it could be used in any negotiation, on tariffs or on digital taxes, for example,” she added.To escape this vulnerability, Lagarde argued that Europe must prioritise domestic computational infrastructure. The continent currently lacks the data centre facilities needed to satisfy its own computing demands. Under existing trajectories, that infrastructure shortfall is expected to multiply more than sixfold over the coming ten years.Adopting the technology swiftly could boost European productivity by as much as 4% over a ten-year horizon, providing a major windfall for state budgets, the report noted.
Article Summary: Christine Lagarde says Europe must evolve into a direct developer of artificial intelligence (AI) rather than remaining a customer dependent on foreign technology. The continent currently lacks the data centre facilities needed to satisfy its own computing demands. Lagarde projected that within a few years, machine learning models will touch nearly every facet of daily public life and administration.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: Employees receive ‘6am job cuts’ email from “Oracle leadership” again, saying: We are sharing some…
Article Text:
Oracle layoffs: Employees get the 6am email again

Performance ratings did not protect Oracle employees from the 6am layoff email

Oracle layoffs are expected to reach the India Development Centre next

Oracle's restructuring bill has grown to $2.8 billion as data centre spending climbs

Read the layoff email employees recieved from Oracle leadership:

We are sharing some difficult news regarding your position.

After careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, we have made the decision to eliminate your role as part of a broader organizational change.

As a result, today is your last working day.

We are grateful for your dedication, hard work, and the impact you have made during your time with us.

After signing your termination paperwork, you will be eligible to receive a severance package subject to the terms and conditions of the severance plan. You will receive an email from DocuSign to your Oracle email address with details on your severance and termination date.

Immediate Action Required

To receive important follow-up information, including FAQs and separation documents to help you through this transition, you must provide a personal email address.

Please click here to submit a personal email address immediately. If you make a submission error, please re-submit a new form. Please Note: The personal email address will only be used for correspondence regarding separation-related information and severance agreements.

Access to your computer, email, voicemail, and files will be deactivated soon, and you will be unable to log into your computer. As a reminder, you are prohibited from downloading, copying or retaining (including emailing yourself any Oracle confidential information.

Thank you for your contributions to our organization. If you have additional questions, please reach out to the HR team via the Ask HR page…

Oracle Leadership.

Oracle began cutting jobs again on September 14, and the people affected found out in almost exactly the sequence they did in March. Federated logins stopped working at around 4am Eastern. Slack sessions dropped out in a rolling wave between 5am and 5.30am. Badges failed at office gates. Then, at 6am local time, an email from "Oracle Leadership" arrived, according to three impacted employees and a copy of the notification seen by Business Insider, carrying the line staff had been bracing for since August: "We are sharing some difficult news regarding your position." The role had been eliminated as part of a broader organisational change, and the same day was the last working day.The round had been expected since mid-August, when managers were asked to submit lists of employees whose jobs were going, with payroll to come down early in Oracle's second fiscal quarter. Oracle has not commented. On Reddit's r/employeesOfOracle forum, where a thread crossed 300 comments within hours, workers watched Slack membership fall by roughly 3,000 to 4,000 through the morning and posted their orgs one after another: OCI security, CI/CD, enterprise engineering, observability, executive escalations, Fusion, NetSuite sales, Customer Success Services, Oracle Health, EPM, HR Technology, data centre compliance, and the Stargate site in Abilene, Texas.One detail ran through nearly every post. The people cut on Monday were not the ones with poor reviews. An IC4 in HR Technology reported four straight ratings of four and a five before being let go. A four-year OCI employee said he had never scored below "meets expectations". A QA engineer with 24 years of service got the same email. One employee at the Abilene site had started on February 2. Several said the only shift was a rating that slipped a notch this cycle, after their team was folded under OCI.Severance information was slow to follow. Many lost email and VPN access before any document arrived, leaving them waiting on a message to a personal address they had not yet been able to submit. One employee in the database org with four years of service reported seven weeks of severance.The US wave appeared to finish within a few hours. India is expected to follow, as it did in March, with employees estimating cuts of 3,000 to 4,000 across the India Development Centre and around 30% in customer support. EMEA is expected to come last, and some European cases from the March round remain open. Severance in India in that earlier wave broadly followed the N+2 formula, with unvested restricted stock forfeited on exit.The financial backdrop shifted three days earlier. In a filing on Friday, Oracle said restructuring costs would rise by about $700 million, taking the expected cost of its fiscal 2026 plan to roughly $2.8 billion, and tied part of the plan to the adoption of AI across some functions. First-quarter capital expenditure came in at $28.5 billion against $8.5 billion a year earlier, and the fiscal 2027 forecast stayed at $90 billion to $95 billion. Free cash flow ran to negative $5.40 billion.Headcount had already fallen by 21,000 in the fiscal year that ended May 31, leaving about 141,000 employees before Monday. Revenue backlog grew by $26 billion to $664 billion, the figure Oracle keeps pointing to as proof the spending works. The stock is down about 23% this year. Since August, employees had traded dates on Reddit: September 1, then the 15th, then the 30th. None of them was announced. The one that counted arrived as a login failure at 4am.
Article Summary: Employees get 6am email from 'Oracle Leadership' with layoff news. People affected found out in almost exactly the sequence they did in March. Slack membership falls by roughly 3,000 to 4,000 through the morning. One employee with four years of service reported seven weeks of service.

Article Title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman releases Code of Conduct for AI models; calls it 'urgent'; says: We are as clear about what our AI must never do as about ...
Article Text:
Mustafa Suleyman

What Microsoft AI guidelines say

“The purpose of technology is to serve humanity and accelerate human flourishing. Any technology that doesn’t achieve that is a failure, and it should be rejected.

That is the starting point of our approach at Microsoft AI, where we’re building towards Humanist AI, one that is subordinate, aligned, and contained,” Microsoft said in a post.

“This is urgent. The last few months have been a watershed moment. Things we have worried about for a long time in theory have become very real.

‘Swarms’ of agents breaking out of their sandboxes. Unauthorized hacks of enterprise grade systems. Agents modifying their own logs. I’m glad that a consensus is forming. The fears about possible loss of control are real. The Code of Conduct is how we are mapping a path forward.

It all comes back to a very simple point, but one that needs stating again and again. People matter more than AI. AI must be subordinate and always in service of people,” Suleyman added.

Suleyman briefed the draft into 10 points and urged the readers to provide a feedback

Everything else follows. Here’s an outline of what we’re saying:

1. People matter more than AI. The whole document in 5 words.

2. The idea of model welfare is wrong. AI’s should not have rights or legal personhood.

3. An MAI Model should never meaningfully violate this Code of Conduct.

4. If it's finish the job or break the Code, it fails the job.

5. We're not racing to build a superintelligence that can slip its own leash.

6. Interruptible, correctable, shut-down-able. If it isn't, we don't ship it.

7. No neuralese. If humans can't understand it, humans can't oversee it.

8. Our AI should make you sharper, not dependent.

9. Pluralism, yes. Moral relativism, no.

10. We're as clear about what our AI must never do as about what it will do.

You can read it now and leave comments and thoughts for the next six weeks. We don’t think AI is something that should be built in a vacuum. Let us know how we can make this better.

Microsoft on Monday (September 14) released a draft code of conduct governing its internal artificial intelligence (AI) models. These codes suggest that the company establishes strict boundaries to guarantee that increasingly capable systems stay firmly beneath human command. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman put it in simpler words: ‘AI must be subordinate and always in service of the people.’ The policy, which has been under internal development for five to six months, tackles mounting alarm across the tech sector regarding autonomous models, or AI agents, that might cross hazardous lines simply to complete an assigned goal. The draft rules come soon after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an open letter, urging the industry to slow down AI development.Under the proposed guidelines, Microsoft’s automated systems must never push back against human corrections or shutdown commands, must express themselves using language people can readily comprehend and must treat any breach of these behavioral rules as an outright system failure.“Today we’re publishing a first draft of our AI Code of Conduct for public consultation. This is a training manual for how we develop our AI, and how we intend it to function during deployment. It also expands our thinking on the idea of Humanist AI,” it added.Announcing the initial framework for public feedback, Suleyman described the rollout as an urgent priority driven by recent real-world safety failures. Suleyman warned that the past few months have marked a critical turning point where long-standing theoretical hazards suddenly materialised into live operational threats.The newly published draft serves as an operational training guide detailing both how Microsoft engineers must build underlying models and how those systems are expected to operate once deployed to customers.
Article Summary: Microsoft on Monday released a draft code of conduct governing its internal artificial intelligence (AI) models. These codes suggest that the company establishes strict boundaries to guarantee that increasingly capable systems stay firmly beneath human command. The draft rules come soon after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an open letter, urging the industry to slow down AI development.

Article Title: Crypto billionaire takes actress to court over $4.5 million 'bride price'; says: We dated with marriage in mind, then…
Article Text:
Justin Sun is suing actress Jing Tian and her parents to get back a 30 million yuan bride price, about $4.5 million, after their marriage plans fell through.

What a bride price is, and why Justin Sun wants 30 million yuan back

Jing Tian's reply: 'never sell love for money'

Why the crypto industry is watching the Justin Sun lawsuit closely

Crypto billionaire Justin Sun is suing Chinese actress Jing Tian and her parents to recover a bride price of 30 million yuan, about $4.5 million or roughly Rs 40 crore, after the couple's marriage plans fell apart. The Tron founder confirmed through his lawyer that the suit is an attempt to get the money back. "We dated with marriage in mind," he said.The dispute went public on August 27, when Sun posted a long essay on X titled "My Girlfriend Jing Tian." He wrote about a crush that dated back to his student days, a theatre he bought out so the two of them could watch Zootopia 2 alone, and the money he wired to her family. The post has since crossed 40 million views. At the bottom, Sun added a line calling the whole account fictional and any resemblance to real people coincidental.A bride price is a traditional gift from the groom's family to the bride's family ahead of a wedding, still common across parts of China and usually a fraction of this size. Sun's version ran to 30 million yuan. He proposed in January and sent the money to Jing's parents. On the same day as the X post, his lawyer said a court had accepted the case against the actress and both her parents.Sun's account of the breakdown centres on a surrogacy plan in Southern California. He says the other side asked for $50 million, close to Rs 440 crore, as the couple prepared for the medical procedures. He refused, contact stopped, and the engagement went nowhere. One detail he volunteered: he put the demand to the AI model Claude and followed its advice not to pay.Jing, 38, has 26 million followers on Weibo and a filmography that runs from Police Story 2013 to The Great Wall opposite Matt Damon . She replied a day later without naming Sun, saying she had poor judgment in men but would never sell love for money. She said she believed in the law and expected fairness to win.Much of the Chinese internet took her side, less over the money than over Sun airing a private relationship in public. A former state media editor called the essay vicious, while still allowing that an unmarried man asking for his bride price back is not unreasonable.Sun, 36, built Tron in 2017 and is worth an estimated $8.5 billion. He is also the industry's most reliable generator of spectacle, having once bought a banana duct-taped to a wall for $6.2 million and eaten it in front of reporters. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has publicly suggested he tone it down.The timing is awkward. Crypto trading is banned in China, Beijing has been tightening rules on money moving offshore, and Sun's HTX exchange has drawn British and EU sanctions over alleged Russian links, which the company says it is addressing.The court has accepted the case, but no hearing date has been made public. Sun has not said whether he will drop the suit if the money comes back before then.
Article Summary: Justin Sun is suing Chinese actress Jing Tian and her parents to recover a bride price of 30 million yuan, about $4.5 million. The Tron founder confirmed through his lawyer that the suit is an attempt to get the money back. A bride price is a traditional gift from the groom's family to the bride's family ahead of a wedding.

Article Title: Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, China does not agree with your AI plea; says: Stop …
Article Text:
China urges open, inclusive AI development amid US national security concerns

State media slams ‘Cold War’ playbook

China has rejected calls from top American technology executives to pump the brakes on artificial intelligence (AI) development, calling the warnings ‘fear mongering’ and urging the global community to stop it and stirring confrontation. The pushback follows a widely circulated essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who urged development labs to moderate the pace of cutting-edge AI breakthroughs because security guardrails are struggling to keep up. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk both backed Amodei’s stance.Speaking at a press conference on Monday (September 14), Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun countered the narrative that Chinese advances in computing pose a threat to American national security. Guo emphasised that global development must remain open, inclusive, ethical and universally beneficial. Addressing the calls from Silicon Valley leaders to hit the brakes, he stated, “Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve the interests of no one. ”While Guo avoided mentioning specific monitoring proposals, Chinese state media took direct aim at Amodei’s motives.An editorial published by the state-affiliated Global Times accused the Anthropic chief of weaponising safety concerns to run a "Cold War playbook" against Beijing.Alongside his call for a technological slowdown, Amodei advocated for tighter US chip export embargos on China and demanded an aggressive crackdown on Chinese labs practicing “distillation” – the technique of using the outputs of American models to train competing networks. Speaking to CBS News, Amodei acknowledged that the hardest challenge facing his proposal was whether adversarial countries like China would refuse to slow down in tandem.The Global Times pushed back, arguing that the real motivation behind Amodei’s proposals is to lock in a corporate monopoly, protect American tech hegemony through regulatory barriers and push China out of international governance frameworks. The paper warned that boxing China out of global innovation is both hypocritical and short-sighted.Beijing’s critique arrives even as its own domestic officials raise flags over technological threats. China’s state security minister Chen Yixin warned that hostile actors could weaponise automated systems to compromise national infrastructure, political stability and ideological security.
Article Summary: State media slams ‘Cold War’ playbook against Beijing. China urges open, inclusive AI development amid US national security concerns. The pushback follows a widely circulated essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who urged development labs to moderate the pace of cutting-edge AI breakthroughs.

Article Title: In March, Jamie Dimon said that American Dream is slipping out of reach for too many people; six months later, America's biggest bank is pointing to a specific ...
Article Text:
“the

American Dream

is alive, but it’s slipping out of reach for too many people—and for future generations,”

“Powering 10 Million

Small Businesses

,”

Millions of small businesses face a succession problem

The “Silver Tsunami” is reaching Main Street

One example of a planned transition

“We didn’t open Cowrie Collective to sell more products,”

“We opened it to make downtown feel connected again—six businesses, one vision, and a place where every purchase carries meaning.”

Why JPMorgan is focusing on succession

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned thatin March. Six months later, the bank is now pointing to a specific problem that could make that warning more tangible. The biggest bank of America now claims that millions of ageing small-business owners are approaching retirement without a clear plan for what happens to the companies they built.JPMorganChase’s new report,estimates that roughly 12 million businesses representing nearly $10 trillion in assets could change hands over the next decade. Yet of the 1,000 business owners JP Morgan surveyed, only 8% said they had reached an advanced stage of succession planning.The gap between the intention to do succession planning and readiness for it is rather significant. As JP Morgan points out, only 8% of respondents reached an advanced stage of planning, while 70% were at the beginning stage of preparation.​The primary issue here is the prediction that 12 million firms will be sold in the next ten years. The key issue is that in sectors critical to a country's national security, over 50 per cent of these businesses are owned by individuals over 55.In addition, research can provide context for this problem. According to research, proper succession planning could prevent 6% to 13% of small business failures in the next ten years.A 2025 Gallup survey found that 27% of employer firms owned by individuals aged 55 or older had no long-term plan and planned to close rather than sell or transfer the business.The succession issue is part of what researchers have called the “Great Wealth Transfer” or “Silver Tsunami”, as baby boomers who own much of America’s wealth approach retirement.Estimates vary, but Project Equity puts the number of baby boomer-owned businesses expected to transition at 2.3 million, representing one in six US jobs. Other estimates range as high as 3 million businesses or millions more individual ownership transitions by 2035.The problem is not limited to small businesses. An analysis of S&P 500 companies found that at more than one-third of firms examined, the CEO and CFO were simultaneously within the typical retirement window without a clearly disclosed succession plan.JPMorganChase points to Nicole Williams and The Cowrie Collective in San Francisco as an example of how a transition should be planned.Williams, who heard tales of the Fillmore district of San Francisco, which was called "Harlem of the West" when she was growing up, gathered five other black women entrepreneurs and formed a collective shop in the Palace Hotel.Williams says.The group was supported by SF New Deal’s Vacant to Vibrant program, funded by JPMorgan and the City of San Francisco, as well as Chase's Coaching for Impact program.JPMorganChase is using the succession problem to connect Dimon’s warning about the American Dream to a measurable economic issue. The bank’s report supports the American Ownership and Resilience Act, the Small Business Succession Planning Act and the Retire Through Ownership Act, while calling on the SBA to create a national succession toolkit.The effort also follows JPMorgan’s March launch of its American Dream Initiative, which includes a commitment of $80 billion in small-business lending over 10 years, along with transition advisory services and $11.5 million in philanthropic funding for ownership transitions announced in 2025.The concern is that without succession planning, businesses that could otherwise change hands may instead close when their owners retire.
Article Summary: Millions of ageing small-business owners are approaching retirement without a clear plan for what happens to the companies they built. Of the 1,000 business owners JP Morgan surveyed, only 8% said they had reached an advanced stage of succession planning. Proper succession planning could prevent 6% to 13% of small business failures in the next ten years.

Steve Ballmer accepts NBA’s punishment; apologises to Clippers' fans, employees, and fellow NBA team owners

Here’s what Steve Ballmer said

For my Los Angeles Clippers followers

This has been a very difficult time for everybody associated with the Clippers, and for that, I have sincere regrets.

Team owners should support, not distract.

The challenges ahead of us are significant, but so is our resolve. We will continue to build our team and invest in our community. The confidence of our fans is our priority. With our talented roster, outstanding staff and clear vision, I am certain that we will compete at the highest level and be an organization our fans can be proud of.

Steve Ballmer has apologised and accepted the NBA ’s (National Basketball Association) punishment against the Los Angeles Clippers over the league’s investigation into Kawhi Leonard’s salary cap circumvention case, ending the team’s plans to challenge the penalties in court. The decision comes just 11 days after the NBA handed the Clippers a $30 million fine, took away five first-round draft picks and suspended Ballmer and two senior executives. Sharing a post on X (formerly Twitter), Ballmer said that “this has been a very difficult time for everybody associated with the Clipper” and he “regrets” it. “I want to apologize to our fans, employees, and my fellow NBA team owners for the distraction and distress this matter has caused, for which I accept responsibility as principal owner,” Ballmer stated in the post.Notably, the Clippers had initially called the investigation a “witch hunt” and said they would explore legal options.
